source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
As per the directive from German diplomatic representatives in India, Indian students applying for a German student visa must submit an Academic Evaluation Centre (APS) certificate. The APS office in India has been processing applications since October 1, 2022. This guide provides all essential details on the certification process.
Disclaimer: This guide is for information only and does not constitute legal advice. Always verify information directly with the APS office in India.
What is APS for India?

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
What is APS for India?
The Academic Evaluation Centre (APS) at the German Embassy in New Delhi verifies the academic qualifications of Indian students wishing to study in Germany. APS offices also exist in other countries (such as China and Vietnam), but APS India is specifically responsible for applicants who hold Indian school or university qualifications. The APS certificate confirms document authenticity and is a key prerequisite for both German university admission and the student visa application submitted via VFS. Once issued, the certificate is valid indefinitely.

Eligibility: Class XII Score Requirement for Bachelor's Studies

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Eligibility: Class XII Score Requirement for Bachelor's Studies
According to the evaluation criteria published in the Anabin database, Indian applicants seeking admission to a Bachelor's program in Germany must achieve a minimum overall score of 70% of the maximum achievable marks in the Class XII certificate, regardless of which board issued it (CBSE, ICSE, or any state board). This requirement applies to admissions starting from Winter Semester 2026/2027.
Two admission pathways are available:

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Two admission pathways are available:
- Studienkolleg pathway: Class XII (≥70%) + APS Certificate → eligibility for subject-restricted admission via Studienkolleg.
- Direct subject-restricted admission: Class XII (≥70%) + APS Certificate + at least one successfully completed academic year in a recognized Bachelor's program → direct admission to the same field of study or a closely related subject.
Completing one academic year does not automatically guarantee direct admission — German universities still make the final call.
Recognition Status of Your University

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Recognition Status of Your University
If you graduated from a private Indian university, confirm that your institution holds "H+" status in the Anabin database before applying. Following the University Grants Commission (UGC) accreditation update, APS cannot issue a certificate to graduates of private universities listed as "H+/-" or "H-" — i.e., those not fully accredited by the UGC.

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Note: For distance or online programs, both the institution and the specific course must be recognized by the Distance Education Bureau (DEB) for the entire duration of the course. APS does not accept distance/online qualifications in disciplines such as medical, dental, pharmacy, nursing, law, architecture, hotel management, agriculture or sports — among others. The full list is published on the APS India News page, and applications in these disciplines will not be processed regardless of the year of enrolment or graduation.

As an Indian student, you can apply for the APS certificate in 5 simple steps:
Review the requirements relevant to your case.
Gather all necessary documents.
Register online and fill out the application form.
Pay the processing fee (18,000 INR) — preferably online via CCAvenue.
Submit your application package by courier (printed, signed, and complete).

APS India: Processing times
The APS verification process takes approximately 3–4 weeks after payment confirmation. APS starts processing only after receiving the fee. During peak admission seasons, processing can extend to 6–12 weeks, depending on the volume of applications and how quickly Indian institutions respond to APS verification queries.
Advice Box

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Advice Box
Start checking your online profile regularly around the 3-week mark — once your verification is complete, the status will be updated on your profile and your certificate will be sent by email.
If your application is successful, you will receive a digital certificate (PDF format) via the email address you used to register. These certificates are authenticated by a digital signature and remain valid indefinitely.

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Note: Digital APS Certificates have been issued since April 2023. Prior to this, students received paper APS Certificates. If you are one of the students who have the paper version, do not worry — your certificate is still valid and will be accepted by the relevant authorities (e.g., German universities, uni-assist, VFS).
Warning!
Here are some key recommendations from German authorities for Indian applicants:
- Don't rush! Take your time to recheck the correctness of the email address you provide. If you mistype it, the whole APS procedure becomes extremely complicated.

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
- Check your spam folder regularly. Your APS certificate may land in spam. It's a good idea to check this folder from time to time.
- Do not "bombard" APS India with unnecessary messages. Repeatedly sending the same emails with numerous attachments can result in your address being auto-blocked, cutting off official communication entirely.

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
- Do not modify your APS certificate. APS India explicitly instructs applicants not to rename, edit, or merge the certificate PDF with other files. It must be submitted as a standalone file to universities, uni-assist, and VFS — any modification can break the digital signature verification and cause delays.

Interviews are not always part of the APS application process for Indians!
Normally, those Indian students who are still pursuing their undergraduate degree at an Indian university MAY be required to go through the interview process after their documents have been successfully verified. This depends on the individual profile of the candidate and the decision of APS India itself. If this is the case, candidates will be contacted by phone or email 10–14 days prior to the scheduled interview to inform them of the location and date of the interview.

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Candidates should allow approximately 20 minutes for the interview, during which they will be asked mainly about their academic background. Interviews are conducted in English or German, depending on the candidate's preference (which can be indicated during the online registration process). If the interview is successful, candidates will receive their APS certificate within 14 days of attending the interview.
Note on terminology

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
Note on terminology
Since July 2024, the document issued without an interview has officially been renamed from "Zertifikat" to "Bescheinigung", aligning APS India with the naming used at APS offices in China and Vietnam. Both terms refer to the same valid document and are accepted by all relevant German authorities.
When to apply for the APS in India?
As soon as possible!

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text:
When to apply for the APS in India?
As soon as possible!
Why is this? Because obtaining the APS certificate, the visa appointment and the visa process itself can take several months. To increase your chances of arriving in Germany before the start of the semester, you need to act quickly.

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text: A practical timeline: For a Winter Semester intake (October start), uni-assist deadlines typically fall around mid-July, which means you should aim to have your APS certificate in hand by May. Hence, accounting for 3–12 weeks of APS processing plus time for the visa appointment, applying around 4–6 months before your university deadline is sensible. For a Summer Semester intake (April start), aim to start your APS application in the fall of the previous year.

source_name: APS India — Process for Indian Applicants
text: One important caveat: APS will not hold your application open while you wait for upcoming exam results or additional semester marksheets. Submit your APS application only once you have completed the academic stage that determines your intended admission pathway. If you later complete a higher qualification that changes your admission category, you will need to apply — and pay — again for an updated evaluation.

What are the different types of German student visas?

source_name: Make it in Germany — Student Visa

What are the different types of German student visas?
To enter Germany, you need a visa depending on the purpose of your visit. If you intend to come to Germany for educational purposes for the long term you must apply for a German national visa. However, you must remember that there are three types of student visas depending on the nature of your study programme:
- German student visa

source_name: Make it in Germany — Student Visa

- German student visa
This visa is mandatory for students who have been accepted into universities in Germany for long-term courses. You must also register yourself in the Foreign Registration Office near the place of your residence in Germany within two weeks to get a residence permit.
- German student applicant visa
This visa is valid up to six months from your date of arrival in Germany. A student applicant visa is issued to those candidates who have not yet received the admission offer and wish to be present in person at the university for admission procedures or entrance tests.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Student Visa
text:
- German language course visa
A language course visa is issued to international students who plan to pursue a German language course lasting between three to twelve months.
You can apply for any of these visas according to the choice of your study programme.

Can Indian students work in Germany with a student visa?

source_name: Germany Visa — Student Visa from India Guide

Can Indian students work in Germany with a student visa?
Yes, Indian students can work in Germany on a student visa. When you convert your student visa into a residence permit, you will also receive an additional green paper called a "Zusatzblatt". This paper contains information about your right to work in Germany. In particular, it states that as an Indian student, you are allowed to work 280 days per year part-time (e.g. up to 20 hours per week) or 140 days per year full-time (e.g. more than 20 hours per week).

source_name: Germany Visa — Student Visa from India Guide

In addition, as an Indian student, you are not allowed to work on a self-employed or freelance basis in Germany. However, if you work as a student assistant at a university, there is no limit to the number of days you can work. However, you still need to inform the foreigners authority about this job.
And do not forget that Indian students can get a German job-seeker visa (aka 18-month visa) after completing their studies in Germany!

 Does the dMAT certificate replace anabin or the formal recognition of my university degree?

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:
No. The dMAT certificate does not replace anabin, university recognition or the formal assessment of higher education entrance requirements.
A dMAT certificate does not change the recognition status of your previous higher education institution or degree. APS India will continue to assess academic documents and formal eligibility according to the applicable APS procedure.
Applicants are strongly advised to check the status of their previous higher education institution and degree in anabin before registering for the dMAT and before submitting their APS application.

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details

D. APS procedure and dMAT certificate
 Does the dMAT certificate replace the APS verification?

No. APS India will continue to verify the authenticity and formal plausibility of academic documents according to the existing APS procedure.
The dMAT certificate does not replace APS document verification. It is an additional element in the APS documentation process and provides a separate academic test result issued by g.a.s.t.
 Does the dMAT certificate replace my university grades?

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:
No. The dMAT certificate does not replace university grades, transcripts or degree certificates.
It provides an additional academic test result and should be understood as one element of the overall application documentation.
 Will I automatically be denied an APS certificate if I submit a low dMAT score?

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:
No. The dMAT is not a stand-alone pass/fail test for the APS certificate.
APS India verifies the authenticity and formal plausibility of academic documents. The dMAT certificate provides a required additional academic test result issued by g.a.s.t. and forms part of the APS documentation for the affected applicant groups.
A low dMAT score does not automatically lead to a refusal of the APS certificate. The APS certificate will document the APS verification result and, where applicable, reflect the dMAT result as part of the applicant’s APS documentation.

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:
No. The score shown on the dMAT certificate does not determine whether the APS documentation is complete.
If the dMAT requirement applies to your applicant group, the dMAT certificate itself is required. Applicants may submit their APS application documents before the dMAT certificate is available, but APS India can only complete the APS procedure after the required dMAT certificate has been submitted.
The completeness of the APS documentation also depends on the submission of all other documents required under the applicable APS procedure.
 Will the dMAT score appear on my APS certificate?

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:
Yes. For applicants who are required to take the dMAT, the dMAT result will be reflected on the APS certificate.
The APS certificate will indicate that the applicant has taken the dMAT and will include the results as indicated by the dMAT certificate issued by g.a.s.t.
The dMAT result is a required additional academic test result within the APS documentation for the affected applicant groups. It does not replace APS document verification and does not replace the admission decision of the German higher education institution.
 Who issues the dMAT certificate?

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:

source_name: APS India — dMAT Exam Details
text:
If the dMAT certificate is already available, applicants who are required to take the dMAT should submit it together with their APS application documents.
If the dMAT certificate is not yet available, applicants may submit their APS application documents first and submit the dMAT certificate later, once it becomes available. This applies only to the dMAT certificate. No additional or updated academic qualification documents can be submitted later together with the dMAT certificate for the same APS procedure.

You can be given an open-ended residence title in Germany once you have obtained a degree or Doctorate from a German higher education institution and worked in a job matching your qualifications for two years. This arrangement does not apply if you hold a residence permit for research purposes.

source_name: BAMF — Study in Germany Guide

This residence title also enables you to complete study semesters in other EU States. You will find more information on this in the section on "Mobility in the EU".

Contact

 Frankenstraße 210

source_name: BAMF — Study in Germany Guide
text: You can come to Germany for up to nine months to apply to study. source_name: BAMF — Study in Germany Guide

What is Uni-Assist?
Uni-assist (Arbeits- und Servicestelle für Internationale Studienbewerbungen) is the central application service for international students applying to German universities. It processes applications for over 170 German universities, evaluates foreign educational credentials, and converts grades to the German grading scale.

As an Indian student, you'll likely use uni-assist for most of your German university applications. The service acts as an intermediary between you and the universities, ensuring your documents meet German academic standards.

text:
The Technical University of Berlin (TU Berlin) is a prestigious public research university located in Berlin, Germany. Known for its strong emphasis on engineering, natural sciences, and technology, TU Berlin attracts a diverse student body from around the world. This comprehensive guide outlines the Technical University Berlin admission requirements for international students in 2025, covering bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD programs, as well as language proficiency standards and standardized test requirements.
Technical University Berlin Admission Requirements for International Students

source_name: TU Berlin — International Applicants Overview
text:
International students aspiring to study at TU Berlin must navigate a slightly different admission process compared to domestic applicants. Due to varying educational backgrounds, TU Berlin has specific criteria to assess the eligibility of international applicants. The TU Berlin admission requirements for international students include academic equivalency checks, language proficiency tests, and application through uni-assist. These include academic equivalency checks, standardized test assessments, and language proficiency verification.

source_name: TU Berlin — International Applicants Overview

- University Entrance Qualification (HZB): Students must possess an educational qualification equivalent to the German Abitur. For Indian students, for example, successful completion of 12 years of schooling with specific subject combinations or clearing JEE Advanced may be required.
- Academic Transcripts: Certified copies of previous academic records, preferably translated into German or English.

source_name: TU Berlin — International Applicants Overview

source_name: TU Berlin — International Applicants Overview

University fees in Germany
Germany has both public and private universities with different tuition fee structures.
Tuition fees at public universities in Germany

source_name: Studying in Germany — Cost of Living in Germany
text:
Germany has both public and private universities with different tuition fee structures.
Tuition fees at public universities in Germany
You’ll be happy to know that public universities in Germany don’t charge tuition fees for Bachelor’s and Master’s programmes. If you plan to pursue a Master's degree that focuses on a different subject than the one you studied as a Bachelor’s student, there may be some additional fees.
The German free tuition system is available for all foreign students, regardless of their country of origin.

source_name: Studying in Germany — Cost of Living in Germany

The German free tuition system is available for all foreign students, regardless of their country of origin.

source_name: Studying in Germany — Cost of Living in Germany

Student accommodation costs in Germany
According to the German Academic Exchange Service, over 40% of international students live in halls of residence. These are your most affordable options, as they’re publicly funded. Other options include sharing a flat or living alone in a studio. Here’s what you can expect to pay for each:
- Halls of residence: 250-300 EUR per month
- Sharing a flat with others: 250-800 EUR per month for a room, depending on the city you’re in
- Living alone: 450-1,000 EUR per month (Keep in mind that most flats in Germany are rented unfurnished)

source_name: Studying in Germany — Cost of Living in Germany

Many German universities include a semester ticket as part of their semester fees. Known in German as Deutschlandsemesterticket, this is a discounted public transportation pass you can use throughout the country.
Cycling remains a popular way to get around. Many cities have bike rental systems, with short-term rates starting at 1-2 EUR/hour and monthly passes available for 10-20 EUR.
For longer trips, Germany’s Deutsche Bahn train network connects cities in Germany and elsewhere in Europe. It offers discounts for everyone under the age of 27.

Health Insurance for foreign students in Germany
It is essential that international students are covered by healthcare insurance before they move to Germany.
Healthcare cover is mandatory by law for all residents in Germany, even those staying for one semester. There are two types of health insurance in Germany: public healthcare contributions or a private healthcare plan.
Degree students under 30 can register for Public Health Insurance but can also choose Private Health Insurance, while others will need to choose a private plan.

source_name: Germany Visa — International Student Health Insurance

Foreign nationals will need to ensure they are fully covered before they start, in order to gain a student visa.

TK also offers other services for students, and the TK eHealth card is probably the most important.
To obtain a TK eHealth card, policyholders must supply a passport photo via TK's online portal. source_name: Expatrio — TK International Student Health Insurance
text:
Students are completely covered by their TK health policy, whether they take out an eHealth card or not. So it's not essential to do so. However, it's a useful addition to anyone's wallet.

Learn more about the TK eHealth card while watching the video. The TK eHealth card is your identification card when you visit a doctor. It makes it easier for you to utilise medical services in Germany and abroad. Simply present the handy chip card when you receive medical treatment by doctors, in hospitals or by approved therapists.

source_name: Expatrio — TK International Student Health Insurance
text:

TK eHealth card
The TK eHealth Card is a very useful tool for exploring Europe. It entitles you to attend doctors' surgeries and hospitals across Germany, and is also connected to the EHIC network, which provides coverage throughout the European Union.

Many students will need to supplement their grants and savings with employment income during their time in Germany

source_name: Expatrio — TK International Student Health Insurance

Working as a student
Many students will need to supplement their grants and savings with employment income during their time in Germany
And there are plenty of posts available, from catering work to childcare. But before they take any positions, students need to be aware of how doing so can affect their health insurance situation.
As a rule, EU students will be allowed to work for 20 hours a week throughout their studies. Those from outside the EU can also work, and have a quota of either 120 full days or 240 half days every year.

source_name: Expatrio — TK International Student Health Insurance
text:
Students can earn up to €520 per month tax-free, but over that point income tax will be applied. If you breach the working days quota, you will also be forced to pay German social security contributions, and your student status can also be removed.
I work alongside my studies. How does this affect my TK health insurance?
As long as you remain under the working days or hours threshold, your health insurance premiums with TK will be limited as German law requires. However, if you breach the guidelines, the price of healthcare (and living costs in general) can rise immediately.

source_name: Expatrio — TK International Student Health Insurance
text:
However, don't let this dissuade you from working your way through university or language courses. Most foreign students in Germany choose to take part-time work or internships, without harming their subsidized health insurance situation.
For more information, be sure to read Expatrio guide to working as a student. It should provide the background you need to earn and study without complications.

source_name: Expatrio — TK International Student Health Insurance
text:

source_name: Expatrio — TK International Student Health Insurance

PhD course & working
Remember that if you earn over €520 per month during your PhD course, you will be classed as "employed". This means that you will need to pay contributions for nursing care and social security, just like any other German worker.

text:
How To Register An Apartment In Germany [2026 Guide]
Contents
If you are moving to Germany, one of the first things you need to do is register your address with the local authorities. This process is called the Anmeldung, and it is a legal requirement for everyone living in Germany for longer than three months.
This guide covers everything you need to know about the Anmeldung in 2026: what documents you need, how to book your appointment, and what happens after you register. We also cover re-registration (Ummeldung) and deregistration (Abmeldung).
What is an Anmeldung?

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
What is an Anmeldung?
The Anmeldung is the process of registering your residential address (Wohnsitz) with Germany's local registration office. It is required by the Federal Registration Act (Bundesmeldegesetz, or BMG). Every person living in Germany, whether German or international, must register their address.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
You must complete your Anmeldung within 14 days of moving into your new residence. The countdown starts from the day you physically move in. Failing to register on time can result in a fine of up to 1,000 euros under Section 54 of the Bundesmeldegesetz, although in practice, first-time delays are rarely penalized if you register as soon as you have stable accommodation.
The Anmeldung is also a prerequisite for nearly everything else you need to do in Germany. Without your registration confirmation (Meldebescheinigung), you will not be able to:
- Open a bank account

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
- Open a bank account
- Receive your tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer)
- Apply for a residence permit
- Enroll in health insurance
How to book an Anmeldung appointment
In most German cities, you need to book an appointment at your local Citizens' Registration Office (Burgeramt or Einwohnermeldeamt). You can usually do this online through your city's official website.
Here are the direct links for some major cities:
For other cities, search for your city name followed by "Anmeldung" or "Wohnsitz anmelden" (for example, "koeln.de Anmeldung").

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
For other cities, search for your city name followed by "Anmeldung" or "Wohnsitz anmelden" (for example, "koeln.de Anmeldung").
In large cities like Berlin, Munich, and Frankfurt, appointment slots often fill up weeks in advance. Cancellations are usually released early in the morning, so try checking the online booking system between 6:00 and 9:00 a.m. daily. In Berlin specifically, calling your local Burgeramt first thing in the morning to ask about same-day cancellation slots can also work.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
As of 2026, fully online Anmeldung is not available in most of Germany. A small number of pilot programs exist (notably in parts of Bavaria using BundID/BayernID), but the vast majority of registrations still require an in-person appointment at the Burgeramt.
Documents you need for the Anmeldung
Before your appointment, make sure you have the following documents ready:
1. Registration form (Anmeldeformular / Meldeschein)

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
Before your appointment, make sure you have the following documents ready:
1. Registration form (Anmeldeformular / Meldeschein)
This is the official form you fill out and submit at the registration office. You can usually download it from your city's website in advance and complete it at home. Even if you use an English translation to understand the fields, the version you sign and submit must be the German original.
2. Valid ID or passport
Bring your passport or national ID card (original). Non-EU citizens should also bring their current visa or residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel).

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
Bring your passport or national ID card (original). Non-EU citizens should also bring their current visa or residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel).
3. Landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestatigung)
This is the most important document after your ID. The Wohnungsgeberbestatigung is a signed confirmation from your landlord (or property manager) stating that you have moved into the property. Under Section 19 of the Bundesmeldegesetz, your landlord is legally required to provide this document within two weeks of your move-in date. Without it, the registration office will not process your Anmeldung.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
The form must include: the name and address of the landlord, the name of the property owner (if different from the landlord), your full name, the address of the property, and the date you moved in. Templates are available on most city websites.
In a sublet or flat-share situation, the main tenant can sign the form if the landlord has given permission. A rental contract alone is not a substitute for the Wohnungsgeberbestatigung. You need both.
4. Rental agreement (Mietvertrag)

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
4. Rental agreement (Mietvertrag)
While not always strictly required by law, bringing a copy of your rental contract is strongly recommended as a supporting document.
5. Marriage or birth certificates (if registering as a family)
If you are registering with family members, bring original marriage and birth certificates. Many offices require certified German translations if the originals are not in German or English.
What happens at the appointment

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
What happens at the appointment
The actual appointment is usually quick, often around five to ten minutes. The clerk will review your documents, enter your information into the system, and hand you a registration confirmation certificate (Meldebescheinigung). This is your proof that you are officially registered in Germany.
Scan or photograph your Meldebescheinigung immediately and keep the original in a safe place. You will need it for opening a bank account, applying for a residence permit, and other administrative processes.
The Anmeldung itself is free of charge.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
The Anmeldung itself is free of charge.
What happens after your Anmeldung
Tax ID (Steueridentifikationsnummer)
After your registration, the tax office will automatically generate and mail your tax identification number (Steueridentifikationsnummer) to your registered address. This typically arrives within two to four weeks. You will need it for your employer and to file taxes in Germany. If you have previously been registered in Germany, your tax ID stays the same.
Broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag)

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
Broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag)
The registration office shares your data with the Beitragsservice (the body that collects Germany's public broadcasting fee). You will receive a letter within a few weeks asking you to register and pay. The fee is currently 18.36 euros per month per household (not per person), and this amount has been frozen at this level through at least the end of 2026. The fee applies regardless of whether you own a TV or radio.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
If you live in a shared flat (WG), only one person per household needs to register and pay. You can set up payment or check exemption options at rundfunkbeitrag.de. Students receiving BAföG may be eligible for an exemption.
BundID (recommended)

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
BundID (recommended)
Once you are registered, it is worth setting up a BundID account. BundID is Germany's central digital identity system for accessing online government services, such as applying for parental benefits (Elterngeld), student financial aid (BAföG), or handling other administrative tasks without an in-person visit. You can create an account at id.bund.de. To use the full range of features, you will need a German ID card or electronic residence permit with the online ID function activated, plus the AusweisApp on your smartphone.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
Re-registering when you move within Germany (Ummeldung)
If you move to a new address within Germany, you need to re-register at the Burgeramt in your new area. This is called an Ummeldung. The same 14-day deadline applies from the date you move into the new place.
You will need the same documents as for a first-time Anmeldung: a filled-out registration form, your ID or passport, and a new Wohnungsgeberbestatigung from your new landlord. Bringing your new rental contract is also recommended.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
You do not need to separately deregister from your old address when moving within Germany. Your previous registration is automatically overwritten when you register your new address.
Deregistering when you leave Germany (Abmeldung)
If you are leaving Germany permanently or for longer than six months without maintaining a residence, you must deregister your address. This is called an Abmeldung.

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
Under Section 17 of the Bundesmeldegesetz, you can deregister as early as seven days before your move-out date and must do so no later than 14 days after moving out. You can do this in person at the Burgeramt, by post, or in some cities by email.
You will receive a deregistration certificate (Abmeldebestatigung), which you should keep. You will need it to:
- Cancel your health insurance
- Terminate contracts (internet, phone)
- Deregister from the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag)
- Apply for a pension contribution refund in the future (if eligible, after 24 months under Section 210 SGB VI)

source_name: Make it in Germany — Housing & Address Registration (Anmeldung)
text:
- Apply for a pension contribution refund in the future (if eligible, after 24 months under Section 210 SGB VI)
Since November 2016, you no longer need a landlord confirmation (Auszugsbestatigung) to deregister. That requirement was removed from the registration law.
If you do not deregister, you may remain liable for health insurance contributions, the broadcasting fee, and other obligations as though you never left Germany.
